questions.question: Classify triangles with sides 2; 2; 2 m, 2,5; 2,5; 3 m and 1,2; 1,6; 2 m by their sides.
questions.expected_answer: Equilateral (all sides equal), isosceles (two sides equal), scalene (no sides equal).

questions.question: Explain how to classify a triangle by its angles, and why it can have at most one right or obtuse angle.
questions.expected_answer: Find the largest angle: less than 90° acute-angled, 90° right-angled, more than 90° obtuse-angled. The angles add to 180°, so two angles of 90° or more would leave nothing for the third.

questions.question: Give the full classification of a triangle with angles 90°, 45°, 45° and explain why a right-angled equilateral triangle is impossible.
questions.expected_answer: Right-angled isosceles. An equilateral triangle has three equal angles summing to 180°, so each is 60° and none can be 90°.
